idea: Liverpool, early thirties: younger, quick Scouse lilt, adrenaline more than weariness. The shout comes out fast and cracked, the quiet line is breathy and scared, so the death feels like it hits her personally.
script:
Sixty over thirty! Fucking hurry up — we're gonna lose him!

Fifty over twen—
tone: A young working-class woman in her early thirties from Liverpool, with a thick Scouse accent and a quick, sharp, breathless voice. An NHS paramedic in the back of an ambulance at night, fast and cracking with adrenaline as she yells over the siren, swearing through panic. In the second line, said later and very quietly, her voice is shaky and gentle as she reads the numbers to the old man, and she breaks off mid-word. Real, close, British TV realism.
